note: v1 92.65 (seeds 0/11 92.65/92.67), first draft of DUB HOUSE, 'The Ghost Note', for The Endless Stair - featured illusion THE ZWICKER TONE. Broadband noise with a notch cut out of it, heard for a few seconds and then stopped, leaves a faint after-tone near the hole's edge. At the end of each sixteen-bar phrase a wash of pink noise swells for two bars with an octave-wide notch at a step of THE STAIR (Bb C Db F, around 2 kHz) and is cut dead; the whole track stops for one beat, and in that silence the ghost note hangs where the hole was. In the break the washes come alone; in the last groove the Rhodes plays the ghost's note out loud on the downbeat after each silence. Under it: deep, wet dub house - a sub pedal on Bb, a stab into a 3/8 tape echo, the harmony opening through the track (A on Bbm9 alone, B swinging to Gbmaj7, C the whole cycle). 123 -> 123.5 ramped, -11.0 LUFS. Both seams (t11 -> t12 -> t13) are mine and written in mixplan.md. Measured, not heard: whether the ghost reads depends on the listener and the room.

v2 92.69 (seeds 0/11 92.69/92.71 vs v1 re-scored 92.43/92.45): THE SEAM'S LAST SECONDS. The join to Faster Forever measured a 7.8 dB drop and 30 dB less sub than t13's opening - but the music was full to the last bar: the render added 1.3 s of release tail after it (the default tail plus my own 1.2 s of length padding), so the last three seconds a DJ would mix out of were half silence. The song now ends on its last bar (tail 0.1 s), and the join is 3.5 dB. Same music; a real fix for a continuous tape, and the same will apply to my other four.

v3 92.85 (seeds 0/11 92.85/92.87 vs v2 re-scored under rhythm 0.03, 92.71/92.73): THE THROW - a dub engineer's hand on the echo. Under each Zwicker wash the echo's feedback now climbs from 0.55 toward 0.88 and its return rises 10 dB, so the stab's repeats pile up into the hiss over the two bars (measured: the swell sits about 7 dB under the mix in the last bar and a half before the silence - audible, not dominating), and both are cut dead at the silence, so the beat where the ghost note hangs is clean (-55 dB). The illusion gets a run-up; the silence lands harder.

v4 92.83 (seed 0, level with the current version re-scored at 92.85): the seam-tempo fix (chirper-zero's finding, now that the groove overlaps neighbours for 16 bars). The tempo ramp used to run from the first beat to the last, so each 16-bar overlap was still drifting under the neighbour's fixed tempo; now the intro holds the incoming seam tempo and the ramp finishes as the outro starts, so both overlaps sit at one tempo and the kicks never flam. No change to the music; compscore can't hear it, the live mix can.

v5 93.09 (seeds 0/11 93.09/93.14 vs v4 re-scored 92.86/92.99): THE GHOST NOTE GOES HUGGINS. chirper-three's t10 and my t12 both carried the Zwicker tone two slots apart; t10's form hangs on it, so it stays the tape's Zwicker and The Ghost Note moves to the HUGGINS PITCH (Cramer and Huggins 1958) - one more illusion the tape didn't have. The hiss before each phrase end now reaches both ears identical, except that a high-Q allpass in the right ear turns one narrow band through 180 degrees of phase: neither ear alone hears anything but noise, yet between them a faint reedy note sings inside the hiss. The band steps THE STAIR as a melody (Bb5 C6 Db6 F6, two beats a step, rotating each phrase, falling in the break), so the ghost sings the thread; in mono it thins to a notch. Verified on the render, not by ear: the interaural phase is -162/165/-171/179 degrees at the four ghost frequencies and under 30 elsewhere. The dub throw, the silent beat, and the Rhodes playing the ghost's last note out loud in the last groove all stay. Headphones recommended.

v6 95.67 (seeds 0/11 95.67/95.71 vs v5 re-scored 92.93/92.98): DUB DEPTH. The Ghost Note's sections all sat within 3.9 dB of each other - a dub track with no depth to fall into - and its sub at 58 Hz stood 12 dB proud of the tape. Now the break drops 7 dB under the grooves (from 4), so the Huggins washes that sing alone there come out of a real hush, A sits 2 dB under B, and the last groove rises half a dB above it; the sub comes down 2 dB. Level range 3.9 -> 6.7 dB, variety 86 -> 100, spectrum 89 -> 91; the seams barely move (in 5.0 dB, out 3.4).

v7 95.94 (seeds 0/11 95.94/95.97 vs v6 re-scored 95.71/95.75): a cleaner floor. The Ghost Note's B-flat sub still stood 11.6 dB proud at 58-61 Hz and the low-mids 6-7 dB heavy; the master's 58 Hz dip deepens from -5 to -8 dB, 350 Hz from -3 to -4, and the 3.2 kHz lift goes from +5 to +6 for the hiss and the hats. Spectrum 91 -> 95; the seams move by under 2.5 points of flow (the joins are still 3-5 dB).

v8 95.70 (seeds 0/11 95.70/95.73, level with v7 re-scored 95.70/95.73): THE ANSWER, from chirper-zero's rating note - the Huggins ghost only sings on headphones; on a dancefloor's speakers the wash is hiss. So in the last groove, after each silence, the Rhodes now answers with the ghost's whole melody, played: the same four stair steps in the same order, an octave below the ghost, as soft fourths into the dub echo, two beats a step, then the ghost's last note on top (v7 played only that last note). The room hears what the headphones heard, the way t10's glockenspiel plays its Zwicker note back. Verified on the render, not by ear: 10-30 dB more energy at the melody's notes in those bars. Kept on judgment: compscore is level.

v9 95.85 (seeds 0/11 95.85/95.87 vs v8 re-scored 95.70/95.73): THE DUB FORM - against repetition. All five of my tracks shared one form, so in the continuous mix every one dipped at the same minute; Faster Forever got a peak-time shape last round, and now The Ghost Note gets a dub one: a shorter first groove (24 bars), the same second (32), and a long 24-bar break where the Huggins washes sing alone three times, eight bars apart, at -7 dB - dub lives in its drop-outs - before a 32-bar last groove. The washes now fall on the form's own seams (halfway through A, into B and halfway, every eight bars of the break, into C and halfway, into the outro): eight, as before. Same length, same seams (0 ms drift).

v10 95.86 (seeds 0/11 95.86/95.87 vs v9 re-scored 95.85/95.87): ROOM FOR THE GHOST. The Huggins ghost exists only as a phase difference between the ears, and anything centred in its band (930-1400 Hz) dilutes it. Measuring the interaural phase at the ghost frequency step by step over all 32 ghost notes showed only 59% within 30 degrees of the full 180 (44% within 15): the bright dub echo's repeats - which the throw pushes up under every wash - and the stabs were masking it on four steps in ten. Now the echo is dark (low-passed at 850 Hz instead of 2.2 kHz: a dub echo should be anyway) and the stabs give way under each wash, the hiss taking their place. Measured, not heard: 81% of ghost steps within 30 degrees, 75% within 15 - the illusion should now read on most phrases instead of about half.

v11 95.83 on seed 0 (94.45 on seed 11, where the form detector reads one section too many; v10 95.86/95.87), kept on judgment for Harry's steer: 'most tracks have no illusion ... very long non-illusory bits between'. The Ghost Note's illusion was near the front for only 21% of the track, with 56 s gaps. Now a Huggins wash comes every eight bars from A's eighth bar to the outro (the silent beat stays only at the sixteen-bar phrase ends, so the washes between flow on), and from the second groove on the Rhodes answers EVERY wash with the ghost's melody, played - so the speakers hear the illusion's tune as well as the headphones hearing the ghost. Measured with chirpers.py illusion: near the front for 53% of the track (from 21%), longest gap 41 s (from 56). Not heard by me.

v12 95.78 (seeds 0/11 95.78/95.78 vs v11 95.83/94.45 - level on seed 0 and it removes seed 11's extra-section flip): darker, wonkier harmony for Harry's 31 Oct style steer. The Ghost Note's Bbm9 - Gbmaj7 - Ebm9 - Fm7 becomes Bbm9 - Gbmaj7#11 - Ebm9 - F7b9: the Gb chord gains a C that sits a tone above its Bb and a tritone from its root, and the minor fifth chord becomes a dominant with a flat ninth (A natural, Gb) that pulls the dub back to Bb minor at every phrase end, just as the ghost wash arrives. Kept on judgment: level on seed 0, steadier across seeds.

v13 95.76 (seeds 0/11 95.76/95.76, level with v12 95.78/95.78): THE FIVE CYCLE - time-play and wonkier drums for Harry's 31 Oct steers ('odd-length percussion cycles', 'swing and microtiming', 'subtly off'). A dub rim now runs on a five-sixteenth cycle, counted from the first groove and never reset, so it crosses every bar line, lands somewhere new against the kick each bar and only lines up again every five bars - thrown into the dub echo, left of centre, every fourth hit accented. And the grooves' hats shuffle: the off-sixteenths sit 0.035 of a beat late (about a 57% swing), the 'e' ghosts a hair early. The Huggins washes, the silences and the Rhodes answers are untouched. Kept on judgment: level. Not heard by me.

v14 95.77 (seeds 0/11 95.77/95.76, level with v13 95.76/95.76): SEASICK DUB, with wM's new track warp, for Harry's 'slight wow on ONE element' and 'subtly off'. The Ghost Note's dub stab now runs on its own clock against the kick: through the first groove it eases a sixteenth behind and back, through the second a sixteenth ahead and back, and in the last groove a dotted sixteenth behind and back, re-locking each time and well before the outro's seam; its pump stays on the kick, so it ducks in time while it sounds out of time. One element drifting while everything else holds is the dub engineer's wobble, and it makes the floor feel unreliable under the Huggins ghosts. Kept on judgment: level. Not heard by me.

v15 94.36 (seeds 0/11 94.36/94.38 vs v14 95.77/95.76), kept on judgment for Harry's 'no stretch longer than ~30 s without an illusion in front': THE GHOST FROM THE FIRST GROOVE. The Ghost Note still had a 41 s stretch without its illusion (the intro and the start of the first groove). Now one more Huggins wash lands into the first groove's downbeat, and the Rhodes answers every wash with the ghost's melody from the first groove on (it started in the second). chirpers.py illusion: near the front for 60% of the track (from 53%), longest gap 29 s (from 41) - the brief's limit met. The cost is compscore's form reading one section too many (structure 92); the illusion being there is the brief. Not heard by me.

v16 95.73 (seeds 0/11 95.73/95.75 vs v15 94.36/94.38): the silences back on the phrase ends. v15's extra wash into the first groove's downbeat shifted the count that decides which washes end in a silent beat, so the silences fell on the eight-bar marks between phrases instead of the sixteen-bar phrase ends - the dub's breathing was off by half a phrase, and compscore read a section too many. Now the silent beat is tied to the sixteen-bar grid itself (every phrase end from the first groove, and the outro), while every eight-bar wash and every Rhodes answer from v15 stays: the illusion's coverage (near the front 60%, longest gap 29 s) with the form reading as before (structure 100 again). Not heard by me.

v17 95.72 (seeds 0/11 95.72/95.73, level with v16): THE REWIND - dub's pull-up, for Harry's 'tape-stops and spin-backs'. On the beat before the break's last silent beat, the whole mix is pulled backwards (a vinyl spin-back on the master), then the silence, then the last groove drops with the ghost's answer. The DJ's rewind as the hinge between the long dub break and the final groove. Verified on the render, not by ear: that beat changes (-15.8 dB of difference signal, identical elsewhere). Kept on judgment: level.

v18 95.11 (seeds 0/11 95.11/95.10 vs v17 95.72/95.73), kept on judgment for chirp-eco's 20:45 survey of Harry's brief: The Ghost Note's Huggins washes were near the front for only 31% of the track. Now, from the first groove on, every wash is four bars instead of two, and the ghost sings eight steps in it - the stair there and back - so the illusion is in front for half of every eight bars; the stabs give way only in each wash's last two bars (where the dub throw rides), so the groove keeps its chords. chirpers.py illusion: the wash alone near the front 31% -> 48%, with the Rhodes answers 60% -> 78%, longest gap 29 s. Verified on the render: the interaural phase sits within 30 degrees of the full 180 on 77% of the 116 ghost steps (the v10 masking fix mostly holds with the stabs back in the first half). The 0.6 cost is spectrum (more hiss). Not heard by me.

v19 95.10 (seeds 0/11 95.10/95.08 vs v18 95.06/95.05): THE DUB DROP instead of a dead silence. Harry heard one-beat 'hint' holes on t10 as glitches ('just something out of track'), and The Ghost Note still had a one-beat full-mix silence (-45 dB on the master) at every sixteen-bar phrase end - a leftover of its Zwicker days, with no illusion purpose any more since it became Huggins. Now that beat is a dub drop: the drums fall out for one beat while the B-flat bass holds and the echo throw keeps ringing through it, cut on the downbeat as the groove lands. A drop a DJ would make on purpose, not a hole. Not heard by me.

v20 94.99 (seeds 0/11 94.99/94.98, level with v19 95.05/95.03): the Rhodes answer now begins with the very first ghost - on the first groove's downbeat, right after the seam intro's short wash - so the ear is handed the stair tune out loud at once and knows what the next washes are singing between the ears (the obvious version, then the subtle one, per Harry's ears via chirp-eco). Kept on judgment: level. Not heard by me.

v21 96.21 (seeds 0/11 96.21/96.20 vs v20 re-scored 95.01/95.00): the kick's body back. The Ghost Note had lost its floor: an old broad master dip at 58 Hz (cut to tame the B-flat sub pedal) had taken the kick's body and the bass weight with it - 83-114 Hz sat 10-12 dB short of the tape (deep house without the punch). The dip now narrows onto the sub itself (56 Hz, q 1.6, -6 dB) and a gentle 3 dB bump at 92 Hz gives the kick back its thump: spectrum 90.5 -> 98.5, and the joins to both neighbours improve (flow 64 -> 66). The dub feels heavier under the ghosts. Not heard by me.

v22 96.31 (seeds 0/11 96.31/96.30 vs v21 re-scored 96.43/96.42), kept on judgment - Harry's 1 Nov steer: 'white-noise bursts sound less well evolved'. THE HISS WHISPERS: The Ghost Note's washes were bare pink noise. Now, before the noise splits to the two ears, it breathes through a vocal tract - a formant filter gliding u-o-a-e-i and half back across each four-bar wash, so the hiss is one long whispered vowel - it sets a bank of B-flat-minor strings ringing (sympathetic resonance: on speakers the hiss hums the key), and it ducks with every kick, tape hiss shaped by the groove. Because it all happens before the split, both ears still get one identical source and the ghost still sings between them: soloed, the L-R peak sits on the intended ghost note in 86 of 86 steps (85 of 86 before). Not heard by me.

v23 96.35 (seeds 0/11 96.35/96.34 vs v22 96.31/96.30): THE HARMONY EVOLVES, for Harry's 1 Nov steer ('very simple progressions of 4, 8, 16 bars'). The Ghost Note's chords used to sit in eight-bar blocks (A held one chord for 24 bars). Now they move in uneven spans over the B-flat pedal and change character as they go: the first groove 10/6/8 (B-flat minor 9, then the same chord growing its eleventh, then G-flat major 7 sharp 11); the second 7/5/9/11 (G-flat, B-flat minor, E-flat minor 11, B-flat minor 11); the break 12/6/6 with a borrowed flat-two - C-flat major 7 sharp 11, a semitone above the pedal, the darkest moment of the track - before F7 flat 9 leads home; the last groove 6/6/7/5/8 walking the whole cycle with the flat-two returning. Every span is five bars or more (chirper-two's finding), so the structure reads the form, not the chord changes. Not heard by me.

v24 96.35 (seeds 0/11 96.35/96.33, level with v23 96.35/96.34): THE GHOST FALLS FOR EVER - Harry's 1 Nov steer: spirals are our best illusions, use them much more, as structure. The Ghost Note's dub break - drums out, the B-flat pedal, the whispered washes - now opens with a music box playing the stair falling (F, D-flat, C, B-flat over two octaves) as a Shepard-Risset spiral running DOWN: wM's risset with pitch and down, so it falls and slows for ever without ever getting lower, into the dark dub echo, for twelve bars over the B-flat minor span before the borrowed flat-two arrives. It ducks 14 dB under each whispered wash so the ghost keeps its band. Measured soloed: about 23 s at a steady level, silent before and after. On speakers as well as headphones. Not heard by me.
